2. Who Can Use CallRoom

CallRoom is intended for licensed healthcare professionals, medical trainees, residents, fellows, students, advanced practice providers (APPs), and other authorized healthcare personnel in the United States who are 18 or older. CallRoom is not intended for use by patients or the general public, and we do not knowingly collect information from patients directly through the App.

By using the App, you represent that you meet these criteria and that your use complies with any applicable institutional policies, including moonlighting, employment, or device use agreements at your sponsoring institution.

CALLROOM IS A PERSONAL WORKFLOW AND ORGANIZATIONAL TOOL. IT IS NOT A MEDICAL DEVICE, CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEM, OR SUBSTITUTE FOR PROFESSIONAL MEDICAL JUDGMENT. NOTHING IN THE APP CONSTITUTES MEDICAL ADVICE. YOU ARE SOLELY RESPONSIBLE FOR ALL CLINICAL DECISIONS.

AI-generated content, including operative notes, case preparation guides, CPT and ICD-10 code suggestions, clinical task parsing, and teaching questions, is produced by automated systems and may contain errors, omissions, or inaccurate information. All AI-generated content requires independent human review and verification by a licensed physician before use in any clinical record or for any clinical purpose.
4. Not an Official Medical Record System

CallRoom is not a substitute for your institution's electronic health record (EHR) or official documentation system. Content you create in the App is for personal workflow management only, the digital equivalent of the paper index cards and pocket notes residents have always used, and does not constitute an official medical record. You must not use CallRoom as your institution's official documentation system.
5. Patient Data and Your HIPAA Obligations

CallRoom does not currently operate as a HIPAA-covered entity or business associate for individual user accounts. You are solely responsible for ensuring your use of the App complies with HIPAA, your institution's privacy and security policies, and all applicable federal and state laws.

CallRoom is designed to minimize entry of direct patient identifiers. When entering Board or Note content, use room numbers, bed numbers, or initials rather than full names, dates of birth, or medical record numbers. You are responsible for exercising professional judgment about what clinical detail is appropriate to enter, consistent with your institution's policies and applicable law.
If your institution requires a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) before using CallRoom at the program or enterprise level, contact legal@callroom.md before institutional deployment.
6. Your Account and Authentication

You may create an account using email and password, Google Sign-In, or Apple Sign-In. You are responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of your credentials and for all activity under your account. Biometric authentication (Face ID / Touch ID) is handled entirely by your device's operating system via the device Secure Enclave, we never access, receive, or store biometric data. If you suspect unauthorized access, notify us immediately at support@callroom.md.

Shared or downloaded Plugins are not reviewed, vetted, or endorsed by the Company unless explicitly distributed through an official CallRoom Marketplace review process, if and when one exists.

Plugins may access external websites and network services. Plugin content is not sandboxed from network access. A Plugin, including one shared with you by another user, could transmit data to, or retrieve content from, third-party servers outside the Company’s control and outside any Business Associate Agreement covering CallRoom’s core infrastructure.
You acknowledge and agree that:

items: You install, accept, run, and share Plugins entirely at your own risk;
You will never enter patient-identifiable information into any Plugin, regardless of source;
The Company is not liable for any data exposure, security incident, or harm arising from a Plugin’s access to external networks or services;
You are responsible for reviewing a Plugin’s behavior before use, particularly Plugins received from other users.
